messages.content: We’re looking at Santa Fe for spring break, probably Sunday through Thursday, driving from Dallas. It would be me, my spouse, and our 14-year-old in one room. Can you compare staying near the Plaza with somewhere quieter a little farther out?
Yes. What dates are you considering, and do you need two beds? I’ll compare the full stay totals, including taxes, parking, occupancy charges, and any mandatory hotel or resort fees.

March 9 through March 13, so four nights. Two queen beds would be best. There’s a chance our daughter’s school arts rehearsal will run Sunday, though, and then we’d arrive Monday and only stay three nights.

Understood. I’ll price both March 9–13 and March 10–13 for one room with two queens and three registered guests. For location, are you picturing a hotel where you can walk to the Plaza, or would a short drive be acceptable if the property is calmer and parking is easier?
That’s exactly the tradeoff. We’ll have the car either way, but I don’t want a cheap-looking base rate that turns into a much higher total after parking and fees.

I found three useful comparisons at the currently displayed refundable rates. La Fonda on the Plaza is the most central. Drury Plaza Hotel is about a five-minute walk from the Plaza. El Rey Court is quieter on Cerrillos Road, roughly a 10-minute drive from the Plaza depending on traffic. I’ll keep every figure tax-inclusive and separate the mandatory charges.
Start with La Fonda. What is the actual total for the four nights?

For March 9–13, a two-queen room at La Fonda is showing $1,356 in room charges, $211 in taxes, and $140 for four nights of valet parking, for a projected total of $1,707. The rate page does not show a separate resort or destination fee. Three guests are permitted in this room, and no extra-person charge appears when the 14-year-old is included in the search.
Is valet the only parking option there, and what happens if we drop Sunday night?

The hotel listing presents valet as its on-site parking option at $35 per night. Public garages may cost less, but I would not count on them for the booking comparison. For March 10–13, the room portion rises slightly per night: $1,047 room, $163 tax, and $105 valet, totaling $1,315 for three nights. So removing Sunday saves $392, not exactly one quarter, because the nightly rates differ.
Okay. How does Drury compare? Include anything mandatory, even if it’s called a service charge.

Drury Plaza is showing $1,196 in room charges and $186 in tax for four nights. Self-parking is $28 per night, adding $112. There is no resort, destination, or mandatory service fee shown, so the four-night total is $1,494. The two-queen room allows three guests without an added occupancy charge. The displayed rate also includes breakfast and the evening food-and-drink reception, but I have not assigned those inclusions a dollar value.
And for Monday to Thursday?

For March 10–13, Drury comes to $906 room, $141 tax, and $84 parking, or $1,131 total. That is $363 less than the four-night version. Compared with La Fonda on the same three-night dates, Drury is $184 less and remains within an easy walk of the Plaza.
Now the quieter option. Is El Rey genuinely cheaper once everything is included?

For four nights, El Rey Court shows $956 in room charges and $149 in taxes. Self-parking is included. The booking screen adds a mandatory amenity fee of $25 per night, or $100, plus $16 in tax on that fee. The full four-night total is therefore $1,221. The two-queen room accepts two adults and one child without an additional occupancy charge.
So it is cheaper, but there is a fee. What does the three-night version look like?

March 10–13 is $747 room, $116 tax, $75 in amenity fees, and $12 tax on those fees, for $950 total. That saves $271 versus the four-night stay. For the three-night schedule, El Rey is $181 below Drury and $365 below La Fonda.
Can you put all six totals together? I’m losing track of the room-versus-parking pieces.

Four nights, March 9–13: La Fonda $1,707 total, including $140 valet; Drury Plaza $1,494 total, including $112 self-parking; El Rey Court $1,221 total, including the taxed amenity fee and free parking. Three nights, March 10–13: La Fonda $1,315, including $105 valet; Drury Plaza $1,131, including $84 self-parking; El Rey Court $950, including the taxed amenity fee and free parking. All six totals include the currently displayed taxes and three-person occupancy.
I don’t think La Fonda is worth that gap for us. Between Drury and El Rey, what are we giving up by taking the cheaper one?

The main sacrifice is walkability. From Drury, you can leave the car parked for Plaza museums, shops, and many restaurants. From El Rey, most Plaza outings will involve driving, finding parking, or using a rideshare. El Rey is quieter and has simpler free parking, but its amenity fee is mandatory even if you do not use the pool or other included facilities. Drury costs $273 more for four nights or $181 more for three nights, and that premium mainly buys the central location plus the included breakfast and evening reception.

Our daughter may be tired after the drive, so not having to hunt for dinner the first night has some appeal. But Sunday may disappear anyway. Are both rates refundable while we wait on rehearsal timing?

The rates I compared are labeled refundable, but their deadlines differ. Drury currently allows cancellation without charge until 11:59 p.m. local hotel time on March 7. El Rey’s rate shows free cancellation until 3:00 p.m. local time on March 6; after that, the stated penalty is one night plus tax. These terms need to be rechecked on the final payment page because rate rules can change.
Give me a practical recommendation, but don’t choose the dates yet. We should know about the rehearsal within a few days.

Hold the refundable Drury Plaza two-queen room for March 9–13 if the reservation permits shortening the stay without repricing or penalty. It is the stronger middle option: walkable location, no resort or destination fee, room capacity for all three guests, and a four-night total of $1,494 including parking. If the rehearsal forces a Monday arrival, the currently displayed three-night equivalent is $1,131. Before reserving, confirm the cancellation deadline, whether changing arrival from Sunday to Monday preserves the live nightly rates, the $28 nightly parking charge, the absence of mandatory fees, and that two adults plus one 14-year-old remain included. Keep El Rey as the cost-saving fallback at $1,221 for four nights or $950 for three, with its mandatory amenity fee already included.
